comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C7-C10. Both evaluations rate these correlational findings and IP3R2 KO validation as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency and appropriate statistics; peer reviewers note 'no major concerns' and accept the correlational evidence as valid.

Perfect agreement on claims C11-C13, C49. Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN due to inability to determine causality from correlational data. OpenEval notes C49 is 'explicitly speculative' requiring additional validation; Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'Causality is therefore somewhat hard to interpret' and requests neuronal imaging data.

Disagreement on claims C14-C19, C52. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing experimental rigor with appropriate controls. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 questioning whether results demonstrate natural regulation ('sufficiency...but does not conclusively demonstrate that sleep is regulated through these pathways in natural behavior') and raising concerns about inverse relationship interpretation. Peer review includes additional claims C4, C58 not in OpenEval grouping.

Agreement on claims C20-C22. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes sound methodology with some subjectivity in thresholds; peer reviewers acknowledge these findings as part of rigorous analyses without raising concerns. Peer review does not include C58 in this grouping.

Perfect agreement on claims C23-C25. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional changes and IP3R2 validation; Reviewer 2 acknowledges these transition-related dynamics as accepted correlational evidence without challenge.

Disagreement on claims C26-C31, C54-C56. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite acknowledging unexpected findings and small sample limitations. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about: (1) whether saturated calcium represents 'unphysiological' state, (2) overstated conclusions about necessity, (3) lack of IP3R2 KO testing in Gq experiments. Peer review includes additional claims C5, C59 not in OpenEval grouping; OpenEval includes C54-C56 which peer review evaluates separately.

Agreement on claims C32-C37, C53. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes compelling cortex-wide effects with some speculation about 'travelled' interpretation; peer reviewers acknowledge this addresses local versus global concerns and accept the differential remote effects. Peer review includes additional claims C6, C60 not in OpenEval grouping; OpenEval includes C53 which peer review evaluates separately.

Both address ex vivo validation claims C54-C56. OpenEval groups these with in vivo Gq-DREADD results (C26-C31) and rates overall as SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C54-C56 separately as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic exploration while questioning whether effects represent 'unphysiological' state in their evaluation of the broader Gq results.

Both address main conclusion C57 about separable regulation. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting C61 is interpretive framework. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 questioning whether 'astrocytic calcium may be not directly affect sleep duration or depth, but some other signal downstream of the GPCR' and whether effects occur through natural pathways.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C59 (main conclusions). OpenEval groups these with C4, C6, C57, C61 and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C5, C59 as part of Gq-DREADD results (with C26-C31) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about physiological relevance and overstated necessity claims.

Both address control claim C52 (CNO-only without DREADD). OpenEval groups with Gi-DREADD results (C14-C19) and rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing experimental rigor. Peer review evaluates C52 separately as SUPPORTED, accepting the control while editors note questions about CNO efficacy differences between Gi and Gq DREADDs.

Both address anatomical control claim C53 (immunohistochemistry validation). OpenEval groups with remote cortical effects (C32-C37) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C53 separately as SUPPORTED, accepting it supports interpretation of remote effects being due to network propagation.

Both address claim C60 (remote cortical effects summary). OpenEval evaluates C60 alone as SUPPORTED, noting it validly synthesizes remote effects. Peer review groups C60 with detailed remote effects claims (C32-C37, C6) and rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging this addresses local versus global concerns.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C3 (NREM sleep definitions) as SUPPORTED, noting these are established contextual claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims C38-C48, C50-C51 as SUPPORTED, noting these establish rationale from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

Minimal overlap on claim C58. OpenEval groups C58 with waveform analysis (C20-C22) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes C58 with Gi-DREADD results (C14-C19, C4) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to questions about natural regulation pathways.

Minimal overlap on claim C4 (main conclusion about depth regulation). OpenEval groups C4 with other main conclusions (C5-C6, C57, C59, C61) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes C4 with Gi-DREADD experimental results (C14-C19, C58) and rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether effects occur through natural pathways.

Minimal overlap on claim C6 (main conclusion about local/remote effects). OpenEval groups C6 with other main conclusions (C4-C5, C57, C59, C61) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes C6 with remote cortical effects data (C32-C37, C60) and rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the differential local/remote effects.
